title: Deterministic metering for client-supplied pre-tokenized lengths and tokenizer hints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Some customers (mobile SDKs, offline preprocessors, and specialized tokenizers) will pre-compute token counts or supply tokenizer hints (e.g., pretokenized segments, explicit token length metadata, or nonstandard special-token mappings) to reduce latency or bandwidth. The metering pipeline currently assumes server-side tokenization and canonical token counts. When we accept external token hints we risk double-counting, undercounting, or non-deterministic billing when the server tokenizer diverges from the client's heuristic (custom vocab overlays, role tokens, or quoting behaviors).

Goal: Provide deterministic, auditable metering when clients supply pre-tokenized lengths or tokenizer hints. Support two safe modes: 1) "client-declared" lever where we accept a client-supplied token_count header as a provisional hint but always reconcile with server tokenization before final billing; 2) "trusted-pretokenized" opt-in for enterprise customers with signed pretokenization manifests and KMS-backed provenance where we can bill directly from the client-supplied counts if verification passes.

Why unique: Existing tickets address stream fragment attribution, speculative decoding, and compressed multipart streams, but we have no systematic approach for client-side token hints and the provenance/verification modes required by enterprise offline preprocessors and low-latency mobile workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Server defaults continue to use server-side tokenization for all billing unless client supplies token hints.

When client supplies token_count header without signed manifest, pipeline treats it as provisional and reconciles against server tokenization before final ledger commit; provisional charges are visible in Console under 'provisional' state.

Trusted-pretokenized opt-in is available via account setting and requires signed manifest + request signature; when enabled, ledger uses client counts as authoritative and stores verification proof in the audit trail.

Mismatch handling rules: if reconciliation delta > 5% for provisional hints, flag as 'reconciliation-failure' and open an audit entry; do not silently apply client counts to final billing unless trusted-pretokenized is enabled.
All new flows emit tracing and metric tags: metering.client_hint.provided, metering.client_hint.mode, metering.client_hint.reconciled_delta_percent.
Unit and integration tests cover: pretokenized inputs, token_count header missing, signed manifest validation failures, and reconciliation edge cases with out-of-vocab tokens.
Console displays provisional vs final token counts in per-request traces for 90 days when hints were supplied.
No regression in existing streaming and multipart metering tests (run full metering CI suite).
Security review completed for trusted-pretokenized path (KMS use, signature verification), and release gated on design review approval.
Rollout staged: internal beta (internal accounts), opt-in pilot customers, then enable platform-wide for accounts without opt-in only as provisional hints (no authoritative billing).
design_decisions: 1) Default behavior is server-side tokenization to preserve current guarantees. 2) Provisional hinting is allowed to reduce upstream latency for clients that want earlier feedback; final ledger commit must be reconciled with server tokenization except for 'trusted-pretokenized' accounts. 3) Trusted path requires a signed manifest: (sha256 of token sequence + model_id + timestamp) signed with account key; verification performed in metering ingest before ledger allocation. 4) For streamed responses with incremental token hints, provisional credits are allocated with a 'provisional' flag and an expiry TTL (48 hours) after which unsatisfied reconciliation will trigger automated refund/adjustment workflow. 5) Keep the verification path pluggable to support future hardware KMS/HSM flows.
implementation_notes:
- Ingest layer: accept optional headers: X-Client-Token-Count, X-Client-Token-Manifest, X-Client-Signature. Validate sizes (max token count 1e7) and reject malformed manifests.
- Metering pipeline: add 'hint_mode' field to the request context: none | provisional | trusted. Provisional path stores provisional_delta in Redis cache keyed by request-id. The finalizer computes server_count and reconciles.
- Ledger commit: add 'provisional' boolean and 'verification_proof' string (base64) to audit entry. Store reconciliation deltas in audit_shard table for downstream analytics.
- Backcompat: if header present but malformed, log and treat as none. Do not change existing tokenization implementation.
- Security: signature verification implemented using account public keys from secrets store; rotate keys handled by existing KMS rotation service.
- Performance: reconciliation happens asynchronously for streaming flows, but final commit must wait for server tokenization for provisional hints. For trusted accounts, skip server tokenization step for billing to reduce cost: still run light tokenization sampling for QA with low rate (1%).
tests_and_validation:
- Unit tests for manifest parsing and signature verification with valid/expired/invalid keys.
- Integration tests simulating: (a) client pretokenized shorter token_count than server tokenizer (b) longer token_count (c) identical counts (d) streamed incremental hints vs final server tokenization.
- Fuzz tests with custom token vocab overlays to ensure reconciliation delta detection.
- Load test: ensure provisional path adds <2% p99 latency to ingest path; trusted path removes server-tokenization for billing so reduces billing latency.
- Audit replay test: replay real request traces from production (anonymized) and verify no net-charge drift beyond epsilon after reconciliation rules.
- Add e2e test asserting Console shows provisional then final values.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge feature flags gated behind metering.client_hints feature flag.
2) Internal dogfood (week 1): enable for internal accounts; monitor reconciliation metrics and audit entries.
3) Pilot (weeks 2-3): opt-in customers (2-3 tenants) with signed manifests. Collect signed verification proofs and customer feedback.
4) Global release (week 5): enable provisional accept for all accounts, trusted path remains opt-in.
5) Post-release (30 days): evaluate reconciliation failure rate; if <0.1% trusted path coverage, begin targeted outreach to high-volume customers.
6) Full deprecation of provisional-only billing (NO) — we do not plan to trust unsigned client counts for billing by default.
monitoring_and_dashboards:
- New Grafana panel: 'Client token-hint ingestion' with metrics: total_hints, provisional_hints, trusted_hints, reconciliation_failure_rate, avg_reconciled_delta_pct.
- Traces: sampled request traces show provisional_count and final_count side-by-side.
- Alerting: P1 if reconciliation_failure_rate > 1% for > 15m across production; P0 if reconciled_delta_percent median > 15% for > 30m.
- Console: add column in per-request trace view 'client_token_hint' and hovercard with verification_proof when present.
- Billing QA job: nightly job that samples 1k transactions with hints and computes delta distribution; send report to billing-ops channel.
